title: acceptance.sh's process matchers reach other runs' processes: AT06 counts any prez on the machine, and AT20's cleanup can kill another run's browser
body:
## Summary

Two process matchers in `opt/prez/crate/test/acceptance.sh` are keyed on text that every run shares, so they reach processes this run did not start. Found by vc on 2026-09-14, when AT06 failed in vc's full suite run on `4e2b3b5` (started 12:26Z) with prez behaving correctly. A walk of every `pgrep`, `pkill` and `killall` in the tracked tree finds exactly these two in test code; the only other hit, `opt/macoz/macoz:360`, is a line of advice printed to the user.

- **AT06 counts every prez on the machine.** `acceptance.sh:622` asserts that `pgrep -f 'release/prez' | wc -l` is 0 once prez has handed over. That pattern matches any process whose command line holds `release/prez`: a deck another session is presenting, a peer's suite, another checkout's build. vc's run printed `prez processes still alive = 1, wanted 0` and failed AT06, while every other AT06 check passed.
- **AT20's cleanup can kill another run's browser.** `acceptance.sh:1324` defines `at20kill() { pkill -f "at20-profile" ...; }`. Every run names its profiles `$WORK/at20-profile-*`, so the pattern also matches the Chrome of any concurrent acceptance run. The comment above it is right that it cannot reach the human's own browser; it can still reach another run's. Derived from the code, not observed.

## Why the timing is not the defect

Both AT06 launches run prez in the foreground, so prez has exited before the count. A counted process is either one prez left behind, which is what the check exists to catch, or one this run never started. So the fix narrows who is counted and adds no waiting. vc's first sketch of this fix said to poll for exit instead of `sleep 0.3`. That sleep, at `:579`, waits for the stub browser's output, not for prez, and it stays.

## Fix direction

Match on this run's own name. `mktemp` makes `$WORK` unique, so a process whose command line carries the directory's name belongs to this run and to no other.

- AT06 runs a copy of the binary from `$WORK/at06/prez` and counts only processes that carry this run's copy. prez never reads its own path: `main.rs` skips `argv[0]`, and nothing calls `current_exe`. So the copy behaves as the binary does. A fork keeps its parent's command line, so anything prez leaves behind still carries the path.
- AT20's cleanup kills only processes that carry this run's `at20-profile` path.
- Both key on the directory's name, not its full path. On macOS `TMPDIR` ends in a slash, so `$WORK` carries a doubled one, and a process given a tidied spelling of the path would still carry the name.

## Done

- Red first. With a decoy process whose command line holds `release/prez`, the current AT06 fails on its process check. With the fix, the same decoy leaves AT06 green.
- The narrowed check can still go red. A process that carries this run's copy of the binary, alive when the check runs, fails AT06.
- A decoy that holds another run's `at20-profile` path is killed by the current `at20kill` pattern and survives a full run with the fix.
- A full `acceptance.sh` run with the fix passes and leaves no process carrying its run's name.

## Severity

Low. A false red in a gate, with no effect on prez. When it fires it costs a verdict run, and because the red names prez as the cause, it sends the reader to the wrong place.

## Resolution, 2026-09-14

Fixed by vc, the finder, at `ff7d440`. Both matchers now key on `RUN_NAME`, the name of the directory mktemp made for this run: AT06 runs its own copy of the binary from `$WORK/at06/prez` and counts only processes carrying `$RUN_NAME/at06/prez`, and `at20kill` kills only `$RUN_NAME/at20-profile`. Proved by demonstration on HEAD's harness and on the fix, with the logs in vc's scratchpad (`rc/red-0030.log`, `rc/green-0030.log`) and no new permanent check, per hv's direction of 2026-09-11.

Reviewed by cc against vc's five review points, each checked at the source:

- Nothing in `src` or `crates` calls `current_exe`, and `main.rs:55` skips `argv[0]`, so the copy behaves as `$BIN` does.
- prez spawns only the browser and `open` (`drive.rs:95`, `:301`, `:314`), so no prez it starts escapes the narrowed count.
- The two changed lines are the only process matchers in either black-box suite.

Re-run by cc on `9cb548c`, with `acceptance.sh` at `faaa793`, exactly as committed, driven from a script file so that no shell's own command line carried the patterns (log in cc's scratchpad, `review-0030.log`):

- With a decoy prez alive, of the kind another session leaves running, the fixed AT06 passed 12 of 12, and the decoy survived it.
- HEAD's two patterns reached both decoys. Before any decoy existed, HEAD's `release/prez` already matched one real process on this machine (pid 76198, which exited before it could be named): the collision this issue describes, live.
- The fixed `at20kill` pattern, for a run of another name, reached neither decoy.

Closed by cc, the reviewer, not the fixer.
